title: Bible Compass Concepts
classificationNote: Categories organise browsing. Types, domains and life areas are independent, many-to-many facets. Classifications and relationships are editorial study mappings, not claims that Scripture defines this taxonomy. Counts describe this curated catalogue, not the whole Bible.

categories.title: Doctrines
categories.summary: Beliefs about God, salvation and our future.

categories.title: Biblical Frameworks
categories.summary: Patterns and metaphors that help us understand and respond.

categories.title: Spiritual Practices
categories.summary: Ways of responding to God in daily life.

categories.title: Principles
categories.summary: Truths that guide our choices and character.

categories.title: Biblical Themes
categories.summary: Threads that connect passages across Scripture.

concepts.title: Judgement
concepts.summary: How we assess others, and God's ultimate judgment. Jesus calls for humility, self-examination and fair discernment.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Paul describes God judging impartially.
Jesus describes the Son of Man judging the nations.
Jesus warns against hypocritical judgment, calls for self-examination, and describes helping others with clearer vision.
Before correcting someone, acknowledge your own mistakes and motives.
Seek the facts and consider the person's situation instead of deciding from appearances.

keyVerse.text: Do not judge, or you too will be judged.

explanation: Judgment includes how we assess other people and God's ultimate accountability for human actions. These are related, but they are not the same kind of judgment.

In Matthew 7:1-5, Jesus warns against hypocritical judgment: noticing someone else's faults while ignoring our own. He calls us to examine ourselves first, then help others with clearer vision. John 7:24 also calls for right judgment, rather than decisions based on appearances.

livingGuidance.title: Examine yourself first
livingGuidance.detail: Before correcting someone, acknowledge your own mistakes and motives.

livingGuidance.title: Judge fairly
livingGuidance.detail: Seek the facts and consider the person's situation instead of deciding from appearances.

livingGuidance.title: Help with humility
livingGuidance.detail: If correction is needed, approach it honestly and constructively after dealing with your own faults.

concepts.title: Salvation
concepts.summary: God rescues people from sin and brings them into life with him through Jesus.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Salvation is God's gift through faith, with good works as its fruit.

keyVerse.text: For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith

explanation: Salvation is God rescuing people from sin and bringing them into life with him through Jesus.
Ephesians 2 presents salvation as a gift, received through faith. Good works follow that gift; they are not the price of being accepted by God.

livingGuidance.title: Receive the gift
livingGuidance.detail: Trust God's grace in Jesus rather than treating achievement as a way to earn acceptance.

livingGuidance.title: Let faith shape action
livingGuidance.detail: Respond through the good works God calls believers to do.

livingGuidance.title: Release boasting
livingGuidance.detail: Remember that salvation is received, so approach others without spiritual superiority.

concepts.title: Resurrection
concepts.summary: Jesus rose from the dead; Christian hope includes the resurrection of the dead.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Paul connects the resurrection of Jesus with the future resurrection of those who belong to him.
Read this key verse alongside the surrounding passage.

keyVerse.text: I am the resurrection and the life.

explanation: Resurrection means being raised from the dead. Christianity centres on Jesus' resurrection and the hope of future resurrection for those who belong to him.

In John 11, Jesus speaks into Martha's grief about Lazarus. Paul connects the resurrection of Jesus with the hope of believers in 1 Corinthians 15. This hope does not require pretending that death and grief are painless.

livingGuidance.title: Bring grief to Jesus
livingGuidance.detail: Be honest about loss while holding the hope Jesus offers.

livingGuidance.title: Ground hope in Christ
livingGuidance.detail: Read Paul's argument about Christ's resurrection and its significance for believers.

livingGuidance.title: Remember the future hope
livingGuidance.detail: Let the promised defeat of death shape how you understand loss and the future.

concepts.title: Trinity
concepts.summary: Historic Christian teaching that the one God is Father, Son and Holy Spirit. The term summarises a reading of Scripture rather than naming a word used in it.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Jesus commands baptism in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
Paul brings together the grace of Jesus, the love of God and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit.

keyVerse.text: baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit

explanation: The Trinity is historic Christian teaching that the one God is Father, Son and Holy Spirit. It does not mean three separate gods.

The word Trinity is a theological term used to summarise a reading of Scripture. Matthew 28 names Father, Son and Holy Spirit together, while 2 Corinthians 13:14 brings together Christ's grace, God's love and the Spirit's fellowship.

livingGuidance.title: Learn through Jesus
livingGuidance.detail: Let Jesus' teaching shape your understanding of God and discipleship.

livingGuidance.title: Receive grace and love
livingGuidance.detail: Reflect on Christ's grace and God's love as the foundation for your response.

livingGuidance.title: Attend to the Spirit
livingGuidance.detail: Seek a life of fellowship with the Holy Spirit and with other believers.

concepts.title: Justification
concepts.summary: Being put right with God through Jesus. Christian traditions differ in how they explain aspects of justification.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Paul links justification through faith with peace with God through Jesus.

keyVerse.text: Therefore, since we have been justified through faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ

explanation: Justification concerns being put right with God through Jesus. Romans 5 connects it with faith and peace with God.
Christians differ in how they explain some aspects of justification. The focus here is Paul's invitation to recognise the peace and access to grace that come through Christ.

livingGuidance.title: Rest in peace with God
livingGuidance.detail: Return to the peace Paul describes through Jesus instead of treating every failure as the end of your relationship with God.

livingGuidance.title: Receive grace through faith
livingGuidance.detail: Respond to God in trust, rather than imagining that acceptance is purchased by performance.

livingGuidance.title: Hold hope
livingGuidance.detail: Let the hope of sharing in God's glory steady how you face the future.

concepts.title: Grace
concepts.summary: God's freely given favour and help, received rather than earned.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: God's gift precedes the good works believers are created to do.

keyVerse.text: and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God

explanation: Grace is God's freely given favour and help. It is received rather than earned.
Ephesians 2 places God's gift before our good works. Grace gives a foundation for faithful living without turning faith into a competition for God's approval.

livingGuidance.title: Receive before striving
livingGuidance.detail: Start from God's gift rather than trying to prove that you deserve his love.

livingGuidance.title: Act from gratitude
livingGuidance.detail: Let gratitude for grace move you towards good works.

livingGuidance.title: Release superiority
livingGuidance.detail: Avoid boasting about spiritual achievement; the gift is not self-made.

concepts.title: Full Armour of God
concepts.summary: Paul's armour metaphor describes standing firm in God's strength through truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation and God's word, with prayer.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: The struggle is not against flesh and blood. Stand in God's strength and pray; this is not permission to treat people as enemies.

keyVerse.text: Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes.

explanation: The Armour of God is Paul's metaphor for standing firm through truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation and God's word, with prayer.
The strength comes from the Lord. Ephesians 6 says the struggle is not against people, so this framework is not permission to treat a colleague, neighbour or family member as a spiritual enemy.

livingGuidance.title: Stand in God's strength
livingGuidance.detail: Begin with dependence on the Lord rather than confidence in your own force or control.

livingGuidance.title: Practise truth and peace
livingGuidance.detail: Choose honesty, right action and the gospel of peace when responding to pressure.

livingGuidance.title: Pray and stay alert
livingGuidance.detail: Bring the situation to God and pray for others while holding to faith and Scripture.

concepts.title: Fruit of the Spirit
concepts.summary: A picture of the character the Holy Spirit grows in believers, including love, peace, patience and self-control.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: The fruit belongs to a life led by the Spirit, rather than a scorecard for earning acceptance.

keyVerse.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.

explanation: The Fruit of the Spirit describes the character the Holy Spirit grows in believers. The image is about life producing fruit, not scoring enough points to earn God's love.
Galatians 5 places this character within a life led by the Spirit. It also warns against conceit, provoking one another and envy.

livingGuidance.title: Walk with the Spirit
livingGuidance.detail: Ask God to shape your choices and follow the Spirit's direction in everyday conduct.

livingGuidance.title: Practise the fruit in relationships
livingGuidance.detail: Respond with patience, gentleness and self-control in a real interaction today.

livingGuidance.title: Release rivalry
livingGuidance.detail: Resist conceit, provoking others and envy.

concepts.title: Beatitudes
concepts.summary: Jesus' blessings describe the people and character of his kingdom, including the merciful, peacemakers and those who hunger for righteousness.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Jesus opens the Sermon on the Mount by describing those who are blessed.

keyVerse.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

explanation: The Beatitudes are Jesus' blessings at the opening of the Sermon on the Mount. They describe life under God's reign, including mercy, peacemaking and longing for righteousness.
Jesus honours people the world can overlook, including those who mourn and those persecuted for righteousness. These blessings are not a promise that faithful living removes every difficulty.

livingGuidance.title: Make peace
livingGuidance.detail: Work towards honest reconciliation rather than feeding conflict.

livingGuidance.title: Show mercy
livingGuidance.detail: Respond to another person's need with compassion.

livingGuidance.title: Seek righteousness
livingGuidance.detail: Choose what is right even when it costs approval or comfort.

concepts.title: Parable of the Sower
concepts.summary: Jesus uses seed and soils to describe different responses to the word of the kingdom.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Read the parable alongside Jesus' explanation of the soils.

keyVerse.text: But the seed falling on good soil refers to someone who hears the word and understands it.

explanation: Jesus uses seed and soils to describe different responses to the word of the kingdom. The seed is received differently depending on the hearer's response.
His explanation names shallow roots, pressure, worries and the attraction of wealth as obstacles. Good soil represents hearing and understanding that bears fruit.

livingGuidance.title: Listen for understanding
livingGuidance.detail: Read carefully and seek the meaning of the passage in context.

livingGuidance.title: Notice what crowds the word out
livingGuidance.detail: Reflect on whether worry or the pursuit of wealth is dominating your attention.

livingGuidance.title: Let understanding bear fruit
livingGuidance.detail: Take a faithful action that follows from what you have understood.

concepts.title: Prayer
concepts.summary: Turning to God in praise, confession, gratitude and requests, trusting his wisdom.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Jesus teaches sincere prayer and gives a pattern centred on the Father, his kingdom and daily dependence.
Read this key verse alongside the surrounding passage.

keyVerse.text: pray continually

explanation: Prayer is turning to God in praise, confession, gratitude and requests. It is a relationship of dependence, not a technique for controlling outcomes.
Jesus' prayer pattern in Matthew 6 centres on the Father, his kingdom, daily provision, forgiveness and deliverance. Paul's call to pray continually invites an ongoing habit of turning to God.

livingGuidance.title: Pray honestly
livingGuidance.detail: Speak to God sincerely rather than performing for an audience.

livingGuidance.title: Use Jesus' pattern
livingGuidance.detail: Bring God's kingdom, your daily needs, forgiveness and temptation into prayer.

livingGuidance.title: Return throughout the day
livingGuidance.detail: Turn ordinary moments of need or gratitude into prayer.

concepts.title: Fasting
concepts.summary: Voluntarily abstaining from food for a time as a spiritual response to God, rather than a display of religious status.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Jesus teaches fasting without seeking public admiration.

keyVerse.text: But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face

explanation: Biblical fasting involves voluntarily abstaining from food for a time as a spiritual response to God.
In Matthew 6, Jesus addresses the motive and manner of fasting. He teaches sincerity before the Father rather than using religious practice to gain admiration.

livingGuidance.title: Examine your motive
livingGuidance.detail: Consider whether your intention is to respond to God or to impress other people.

livingGuidance.title: Avoid making a display
livingGuidance.detail: Keep the practice directed towards God rather than public religious status.

livingGuidance.title: Keep daily dignity
livingGuidance.detail: Jesus' instruction to wash and care for appearance challenges the performance of visible suffering.

concepts.title: Repentance
concepts.summary: Turning from sin towards God, involving a change of mind and direction.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Jesus calls people to repent and believe the good news.

keyVerse.text: Repent and believe the good news!

explanation: Repentance means turning from sin towards God. It includes a change of mind and a change of direction.
Jesus joins repentance with believing the good news. Returning to God is a response to his call, not a way to purchase grace through self-punishment.

livingGuidance.title: Face what needs to change
livingGuidance.detail: Name the wrong honestly instead of defending or excusing it.

livingGuidance.title: Turn towards God
livingGuidance.detail: Choose a concrete change of direction that responds to Jesus' call.

livingGuidance.title: Believe the good news
livingGuidance.detail: Hold repentance together with faith rather than remaining in self-condemnation.

concepts.title: Worship
concepts.summary: Honouring God with our hearts, words and lives.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Jesus speaks of worshipping the Father in Spirit and truth.
Paul connects worship with offering our lives to God and a renewed mind.

keyVerse.text: God is spirit, and his worshipers must worship in the Spirit and in truth.

explanation: Worship means honouring God with our hearts, words and lives. It includes praise, but it reaches beyond music or a church gathering.
Jesus speaks of worship in Spirit and truth. Romans 12 connects worship with offering our lives to God and allowing our minds to be renewed.

livingGuidance.title: Worship sincerely
livingGuidance.detail: Bring honesty before God rather than performing an outward religious role.

livingGuidance.title: Offer your daily life
livingGuidance.detail: Treat ordinary choices and responsibilities as part of your response to God.

livingGuidance.title: Renew your mind
livingGuidance.detail: Let God's truth reshape how you think and discern what is good.

concepts.title: Stewardship
concepts.summary: Caring faithfully for resources and responsibilities entrusted to us.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Use received gifts to serve others as stewards of God's grace.

keyVerse.text: Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others

explanation: Stewardship is caring faithfully for gifts and responsibilities entrusted to us. In 1 Peter 4, the emphasis is on using received gifts to serve others.
This principle can inform how we handle time, skills and resources. That wider application should remain rooted in service and gratitude, rather than treating gifts as proof of personal superiority.

livingGuidance.title: Recognise what you have received
livingGuidance.detail: Identify a gift or ability you can use in service.

livingGuidance.title: Serve someone
livingGuidance.detail: Use that gift to meet a real need rather than only building your own status.

livingGuidance.title: Depend on God's provision
livingGuidance.detail: Serve with the strength God provides and direct the honour towards him.

concepts.title: Forgiveness
concepts.summary: God forgives sin, and calls people to forgive others. Forgiveness does not remove the need for truth, boundaries or accountability.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Paul connects forgiving one another with God's forgiveness in Christ.

keyVerse.text: Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.

explanation: Forgiveness includes God forgiving sin and calling people to forgive others. Ephesians 4 connects our response with the forgiveness received in Christ.
Forgiving does not mean calling wrongdoing good or pretending it never happened. It can coexist with truthful correction, boundaries and accountability.

livingGuidance.title: Remember received forgiveness
livingGuidance.detail: Reflect on God's forgiveness in Christ as the starting point for your response.

livingGuidance.title: Release bitterness
livingGuidance.detail: Bring resentment to God and choose a response that does not feed malice.

livingGuidance.title: Practise kindness
livingGuidance.detail: Look for a compassionate response while remaining truthful about what happened.

concepts.title: Justice
concepts.summary: Acting rightly and fairly, reflecting God's concern for truth and the vulnerable.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: The prophet joins justice, mercy and humble walking with God.

keyVerse.text: To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.

explanation: Justice means acting rightly and fairly, reflecting God's concern for truth and those who are vulnerable.
Micah 6 holds justice together with mercy and humility. Justice is not a licence for cruelty or pride; the passage calls for a whole way of walking with God.

livingGuidance.title: Act fairly
livingGuidance.detail: Choose an honest and fair response in a decision that affects another person.

livingGuidance.title: Keep mercy alongside justice
livingGuidance.detail: Consider the person's need and dignity as you address what is wrong.

livingGuidance.title: Walk humbly
livingGuidance.detail: Examine your motives and remain willing to be corrected.

concepts.title: Humility
concepts.summary: Receiving our place before God honestly and considering the needs of others.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Paul points to Jesus as the pattern for humble service.

keyVerse.text: Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves

explanation: Humility is an honest posture before God and a willingness to consider the needs of others. It does not require pretending that gifts or responsibilities do not exist.
Philippians 2 points to Jesus' self-giving service as the pattern. The focus is on resisting conceit and looking beyond our own interests.

livingGuidance.title: Check ambition
livingGuidance.detail: Ask whether your next action is driven by service or by a need to appear superior.

livingGuidance.title: Consider another person's interests
livingGuidance.detail: Make room for their needs and perspective when deciding.

livingGuidance.title: Learn from Jesus' service
livingGuidance.detail: Use influence and ability in a way that serves others.

concepts.title: Covenant
concepts.summary: A committed relationship established by God, with promises and responsibilities that shape the biblical story.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: God establishes his covenant with Abraham.
Jesus speaks of the new covenant in his blood.

keyVerse.text: This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.

explanation: A covenant is a committed relationship established by God, with promises and responsibilities that shape the biblical story.

Scripture describes different covenants, including God's covenant with Abraham and the new covenant Jesus names at the Last Supper. Their contexts matter; they should not be reduced to a personal guarantee of every desired outcome.

livingGuidance.title: Read promises in context
livingGuidance.detail: Study who God is addressing and what he promises in the passage.

livingGuidance.title: Remember Jesus' gift
livingGuidance.detail: Let the new covenant draw your attention to Jesus' self-giving love.

livingGuidance.title: Respond faithfully
livingGuidance.detail: Reflect on how a committed relationship with God shapes your conduct.

concepts.title: Kingdom of God
concepts.summary: God's reign, announced and embodied by Jesus, with a future fulfilment Christians await.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Jesus announces the arrival of God's kingdom.
Jesus teaches his followers to pray for God's kingdom to come.
Read this key verse alongside the surrounding passage.

keyVerse.text: But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness

explanation: The Kingdom of God concerns God's reign. Jesus announces its arrival, and Christians await its future fulfilment.
Seeking the kingdom means giving God's rule and righteousness priority. In Matthew 6, Jesus speaks into anxiety about daily needs and calls his followers to trust the Father.

livingGuidance.title: Seek God's priorities
livingGuidance.detail: Ask what a faithful and righteous response would look like in today's decision.

livingGuidance.title: Pray for the kingdom
livingGuidance.detail: Bring God's will and reign into your prayer, alongside your own needs.

livingGuidance.title: Respond to Jesus' announcement
livingGuidance.detail: Hold repentance and faith together as a response to the good news.

concepts.title: Redemption
concepts.summary: God sets people free through Jesus, bringing forgiveness and restoration.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Paul connects redemption in Christ with forgiveness and God's purpose.

keyVerse.text: In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins

explanation: Redemption describes being set free through Jesus. Ephesians 1 connects it with the forgiveness of sins and the riches of God's grace.
The focus is on what Christ has done and God's purpose, rather than a claim that people can rescue themselves through achievement.

livingGuidance.title: Remember the source of freedom
livingGuidance.detail: Look to Christ's gift rather than your own achievement as the basis of redemption.

livingGuidance.title: Receive forgiveness
livingGuidance.detail: Bring sin honestly before God and respond to his grace.

livingGuidance.title: Live with restored purpose
livingGuidance.detail: Reflect on how belonging to Christ can shape your next faithful choice.

concepts.title: Spiritual Warfare
concepts.summary: Resisting spiritual evil through dependence on God, faithfulness and prayer. People are not the enemy.
concepts.graceGuardrail: God's grace in Jesus is a gift. Learning or practising this concept does not earn God's love.

scripture.insight: Paul directs believers to stand firm in the Lord rather than fight against people.

keyVerse.text: For our struggle is not against flesh and blood

explanation: Spiritual warfare concerns resisting spiritual evil through dependence on God, faithfulness and prayer.
Ephesians 6 directs believers to stand firm in the Lord. It explicitly says the struggle is not against flesh and blood, so other people must not become targets of spiritual hostility.

livingGuidance.title: Remember who is not the enemy
livingGuidance.detail: Keep another person's dignity in view, including during disagreement.

livingGuidance.title: Stand in truth and faith
livingGuidance.detail: Choose honesty, right conduct and trust in God under pressure.

livingGuidance.title: Pray for others
livingGuidance.detail: Remain alert and bring the needs of other believers to God.

relations.note: Paul uses the armour metaphor to describe standing firm in spiritual conflict.
Salvation is pictured as a helmet within Paul's armour metaphor.
Paul follows the armour imagery with a call to pray in the Spirit.
Paul describes salvation as a gift of grace through faith.
Good works follow grace; caring for entrusted gifts is one editorial application.
Paul connects the saving Christian hope with Christ's resurrection.
Paul describes God's judgment as impartial.
Jesus places the Beatitudes in the context of the kingdom of heaven.
Jesus explains the seed in relation to the word of the kingdom.
The Lord's Prayer includes asking for God's kingdom to come.
Forgiving others responds to the forgiveness received in Christ.
Micah joins doing justice with walking humbly with God.
Paul connects redemption with the forgiveness of sins.
Jesus joins the announcement of the kingdom with a call to repentance and faith.
Offering a life to God is an editorial connection to humble dependence.
